T1.why_behaviour_changes: Creators shift from budget brands to Neumann when they perceive a clear value proposition that meets their workflow and quality expectations.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Neumann can capture value through expanded product lines, subscription services, and bundled kits, leveraging its existing brand prestige and academy content to differentiate from competitors.
assumptions: Creators currently avoid Neumann due to perceived high price or lack of entry-level options.
A differentiated proposition will be adopted if it offers tangible benefits (e.g., lower price, specific features, or integrated learning).
The market is large enough to support additional volume without cannibalizing professional sales.
predictions: If offered a differentiated proposition, purchase intent among creators will increase by at least 15% compared to the current baseline.

Creator satisfaction scores will rise, leading to positive word-of-mouth and repeat purchases.

assumptions: Creators value brand prestige as a signal of quality and professionalism.

The Neumann brand is currently perceived as professional rather than consumer.
predictions: If a survey shows that creators rank Neumann highest for perceived professional credibility, purchase intent will increase by at least 15% compared to a generic brand.

arguments.target_customer: Home-studio creators (YouTube channels, podcast hosts, independent musicians) who currently use budget or entry-level equipment.
arguments.value_proposition: A differentiated proposition that addresses creator-specific needs (e.g., affordable entry-level mics, bundled tutorials, or studio-in-a-box kits) while leveraging Neumann’s existing brand prestige and academy content.
arguments.next_action: Execute the Creator Purchase Intent Test (X1) within the €18,000 budget and 10‑week timeline, randomizing participants to either a differentiated proposition offer or a premium branding offer.
arguments.uncertainty: Both T1 (differentiated proposition) and T2 (premium branding) remain uncertain due to lack of direct evidence on creator purchasing behavior and willingness to pay for differentiated offerings.
would_change_if: If the test shows Group B (premium branding) meeting the same purchase intent and WTP thresholds, we would shift focus to premium branding. If neither group meets thresholds, we would consider no expansion or a hybrid approach.
If new evidence shows strong demand for entry-level mics or that creators actively seek affordable options, T1 would become more likely.
If new evidence shows that creators primarily purchase based on brand prestige and are willing to pay a premium for professional credibility, T2 would become more likely.

arguments.claim: Home boat owners will increase purchases of marine coatings if they perceive the product as a premium, protective finish that enhances boat appearance and durability, and if Jotun offers a dedicated retail or online channel.
arguments.who_benefits: Jotun benefits by capturing higher-margin consumer sales and building brand loyalty among DIY boat owners.
arguments.why_behaviour_changes: If boat owners view marine coatings as a fashion or performance-enhancing item rather than a purely functional necessity, they will be willing to buy multiple coats and choose Jotun over competitors.

assumptions: Boat owners in target markets (e.g., Scandinavia, Europe) have discretionary spending for boat aesthetics.

predictions: Surveyed boat owners will indicate intent to purchase Jotun marine coatings at a price 15-20% above standard marine paints.
Sales of Jotun marine coatings in DIY channels will grow faster than B2B sales in the same region.
Customer reviews will highlight appearance and durability as key purchase drivers.

arguments.who_benefits: Jotun benefits by leveraging its existing distribution network to offer personalized guidance, increasing consumer engagement and repeat purchases.

Boat owners value expert opinion and are willing to pay for it.
A community platform can be integrated into existing distribution channels.
predictions: Surveyed boat owners will indicate higher purchase intent when offered personalized guidance.
Sales of Jotun coatings will increase in regions where community support is promoted.
Customer feedback will highlight the value of expert recommendations as a purchase driver.

T1.claim: Home boat owners will increase purchases of marine coatings if they perceive the product as a premium, protective finish that enhances boat appearance and durability, and if Jotun offers a dedicated retail or online channel.
T1.who_benefits: Jotun benefits by capturing higher-margin consumer sales and building brand loyalty among DIY boat owners.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: If boat owners view marine coatings as a fashion or performance-enhancing item rather than a purely functional necessity, they will be willing to buy multiple coats and choose Jotun over competitors.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Jotun can price premium coatings, sell through its own e-commerce or retail partners, and cross-sell related products (e.g., applicators, primers).
assumptions: Boat owners in target markets (e.g., Scandinavia, Europe) have discretionary spending for boat aesthetics.
Jotun can produce a differentiated, visible finish that differentiates it from competitors.
A direct-to-consumer channel can be established at acceptable cost.
predictions: Surveyed boat owners will indicate intent to purchase Jotun marine coatings at a price 15-20% above standard marine paints.
Sales of Jotun marine coatings in DIY channels will grow faster than B2B sales in the same region.

A community platform can be integrated into existing distribution channels.
predictions: Surveyed boat owners will indicate higher purchase intent when offered personalized guidance.

frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient evidence to justify Jotun investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, leveraging its marine and protective coatings technology, based on publicly available information up to mid-2024.
constraints: Limited to public sources available up to mid-2024; no internal company data.

T1.claim: Home boat owners will increase purchases of marine coatings if they perceive the product as a premium, protective finish that enhances boat appearance and durability, and if Jotun offers a dedicated retail or online channel.

T1.why_behaviour_changes: If boat owners view marine coatings as a fashion or performance-enhancing item rather than a purely functional necessity, they will be willing to buy multiple coats and choose Jotun over competitors.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Jotun can price premium coatings, sell through its own e-commerce or retail partners, and cross-sell related products (e.g., applicators, primers).
assumptions: Boat owners in target markets (e.g., Scandinavia, Europe) have discretionary spending for boat aesthetics.
Jotun can produce a differentiated, visible finish that differentiates it from competitors.
A direct-to-consumer channel can be established at acceptable cost.
predictions: Surveyed boat owners will indicate intent to purchase Jotun marine coatings at a price 15-20% above standard marine paints.
Sales of Jotun marine coatings in DIY channels will grow faster than B2B sales in the same region.
Customer reviews will highlight appearance and durability as key purchase drivers.

frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient evidence to justify Jotun investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, leveraging its marine and protective coatings technology, based on publicly available information up to mid-2024.
constraints: Limited to public sources available up to mid-2024; no internal company data.

alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home boat owners, DIY protective coatings).

T1.claim: Home boat owners will increase purchases of marine coatings if they perceive the product as a premium, protective finish that enhances boat appearance and durability, and if Jotun offers a dedicated retail or online channel.
T1.who_benefits: Jotun benefits by capturing higher-margin consumer sales and building brand loyalty among DIY boat owners.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: If boat owners view marine coatings as a fashion or performance-enhancing item rather than a purely functional necessity, they will be willing to buy multiple coats and choose Jotun over competitors.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Jotun can price premium coatings, sell through its own e-commerce or retail partners, and cross-sell related products (e.g., applicators, primers).
assumptions: Boat owners in target markets (e.g., Scandinavia, Europe) have discretionary spending for boat aesthetics.
Jotun can produce a differentiated, visible finish that differentiates it from competitors.
A direct-to-consumer channel can be established at acceptable cost.
predictions: Surveyed boat owners will indicate intent to purchase Jotun marine coatings at a price 15-20% above standard marine paints.

Customer reviews will highlight appearance and durability as key purchase drivers.

frame.objective: Determine whether Tanita should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case based on its stand-on bioelectrical impedance body-fat analyser, leveraging evidence available up to 1993.
constraints: Limited to public sources published before 1993; no internal company data.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Uncertainty about Tanita’s current reach to individual buyers; must be discovered.
Investment decision must be justified by evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, or competitive advantage.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home fitness, weight management, or medical self‑monitoring).
2) Expand the existing B2B offering to additional health clubs or clinics without creating a consumer proposition.
3) No expansion – continue focusing exclusively on commercial scales and existing B2B customers.
4) License the bioelectrical impedance technology to third parties for consumer applications.

T1.claim: Health‑conscious consumers will purchase a stand‑on body‑fat analyser for home use because they view it as a medical necessity that provides actionable health insights.
T1.who_benefits: Consumers seeking to monitor body composition for health management; Tanita benefits by capturing premium sales and recurring revenue from accessories or services.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: Growing public awareness of obesity and its health risks (e.g., heart disease, diabetes) makes consumers seek measurable, professional‑grade body‑fat data as a way to stay on track.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Tanita can charge a premium price for a consumer‑grade analyser, sell accessories (e.g., scales, software), and potentially offer subscription services for data tracking.
assumptions: Consumers trust medical evidence linking body fat to health outcomes.
Tanita’s existing professional reputation transfers to consumer perception of accuracy.
Price sensitivity is low for health‑critical devices.
predictions: Surveyed consumers will indicate willingness to pay at least 1.5x the price of a standard scale for a body‑fat analyser.
Purchase intent will be higher among those who report tracking BMI or body composition at least monthly.
Repeat purchase rate for accessories or service subscriptions will exceed 20% within 12 months.

T2.how_value_is_captured: Tanita can price the analyser at a premium, market it through lifestyle channels, and sell additional accessories or data services to reinforce the status narrative.

X1.name: Consumer Preference Survey for Medical vs Status Messaging
X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants view a product description of a stand-on body-fat analyser either framed as a medical necessity (health tracking, professional accuracy) or as a status accessory (health awareness, lifestyle signaling). They then indicate willingness to pay (WTP) on a 7-point scale and purchase intent (1‑10).
X1.sample: 500 Japanese adults aged 25‑55, recruited via an online panel, balanced for gender and urban/rural.
X1.measure: Average WTP (EUR) and purchase intent score for each messaging frame.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Higher WTP and purchase intent when framed as medical necessity.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Higher WTP and purchase intent when framed as status accessory.

X1.decision_rule: If the average WTP for medical frame exceeds status frame by at least 15% (e.g., €35 vs €30), proceed with medical‑focused consumer proposition. If status frame exceeds medical by at least 15%, proceed with status‑focused prop

final.recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Conduct the proposed Consumer Preference Survey (Test X1) to empirically compare medical‑necessity versus status messaging framing before committing to a product launch. The test will determine whether consumer willingness to pay and purchase intent differ significantly between the two frames, which would justify either a medical‑focused or a status
final.target_customer: Health‑conscious consumers in Japan who track body composition for personal health management, possibly also health‑conscious professionals (clinics, health clubs) seeking a professional‑grade device for clients.
final.value_proposition: A stand‑on body‑fat analyser marketed as a medical necessity for accurate health tracking, with premium pricing justified by professional accuracy and recurring revenue from accessories and services.
final.next_action: Run the Consumer Preference Survey (Test X1) within the €15,000 budget and 12‑week timeline to measure willingness to pay and purchase intent under medical‑necessity versus status framing.
final.uncertainty: Consumer demand for a consumer‑grade body‑fat analyser is uncertain. Evidence shows widespread household ownership of bathroom scales and growing BMI awareness, but no direct proof of willingness to pay a premium for a professional‑grade
would_change_if: If the survey shows willingness to pay at least 1.5x the price of a standard scale for a medical‑necessity framed device, and purchase intent is significantly higher than for a status framed device.
If a separate pilot sale of a limited run of the analyser shows strong pre‑orders or actual sales within 6 months.

X1.name: Consumer Preference Survey for Home Body-Fat Analyzer
X1.method: Online survey with simulated purchase offer. Recruit 500 Japanese adults (aged 20-65) via a panel. Randomly assign participants to one of two conditions: Condition A receives a product description emphasizing home use and consumer convenience; Condition B receives the same description plus a statement that insurance coverage is available. Both conditions see a price of $180 and a brief product demo. Participants indicate whether they would purchase ("Yes"/"No").
X1.sample: 500 Japanese adults, balanced by age and gender, recruited from a panel.
X1.measure: Purchase intent (binary) and willingness to pay (open-ended).

prediction_by_theory.T2: Purchase intent will be higher in Condition B (insurance coverage emphasis) because insurance removes out-of-pocket cost and patients prioritize preventive care.

arguments.name: Consumer Preference Survey for Home Body-Fat Analyzer
arguments.method: Online survey with simulated purchase offer. Recruit 500 Japanese adults (aged 20-65) via a panel. Randomly assign participants to one of two conditions: Condition A receives a product description emphasizing home use and consumer convenience; Condition B receives the same description plus a statement that insurance coverage is available. Both conditions see a price of $180 and a brief product demo. Participants indicate whether they would purchase ("Yes"/"No").
arguments.sample: 500 Japanese adults, balanced by age and gender, recruited from a panel.
arguments.measure: Purchase intent (binary) and willingness to pay (open-ended).

prediction_by_theory.T1: Purchase intent will be higher in Condition A (home-use emphasis) because consumers already track body composition and value private measurement.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Purchase intent will be higher in Condition B (insurance coverage emphasis) because insurance removes out-of-pocket cost and patients prioritize preventive care.

frame.objective: Determine whether Tanita should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case based on its stand-on bioelectrical impedance body-fat analyser, leveraging evidence available up to 1993.
constraints: Limited to public sources published before 1993; no internal company data.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Uncertainty about Tanita’s current reach to individual buyers; must be discovered.
Investment decision must be justified by evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, or competitive advantage.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home fitness, weight management, or medical self‑monitoring).
2) Expand the existing B2B offering to additional health clubs or clinics without creating a consumer proposition.
3) No expansion – continue focusing exclusively on commercial scales and existing B2B customers.
4) License the bioelectrical impedance technology to third parties for consumer applications.

T1.claim: Health‑conscious consumers will adopt a stand‑on bioelectrical impedance body‑fat analyser for home use because they view it as a medical necessity that provides actionable health insights.
T1.who_benefits: Consumers seeking to monitor body composition for health management; Tanita benefits by selling premium home devices and capturing value through direct sales.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: Growing public awareness of the health risks of excess body fat (as shown by medical evidence and media coverage) makes consumers seek measurable data on body composition as a preventive measure.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Tanita can charge a premium for a home device that delivers accurate, clinically relevant data, and sell directly to consumers via retail or online channels, bypassing distributors.
assumptions: Consumers trust Tanita’s medical‑grade accuracy.
Home use is acceptable for privacy and convenience.
Price sensitivity is moderate for health‑related products.
predictions: Surveyed consumers will indicate willingness to pay at least 150% of the professional price for a home version.
Pilot sales of a home version will exceed 5,000 units in the first year if marketed as a health tool.
T1.first_claim: Health‑conscious consumers will adopt a stand‑on bioelectrical impedance body‑fat analyser for home use because they view it as a medical necessity that provides actionable health insights.

T2.claim: Consumers will adopt a stand‑on bioelectrical impedance body‑fat analyser for home use because they view it as a status and lifestyle accessory that signals health‑consciousness and sophistication.
T2.who_benefits: Status‑conscious consumers seeking to demonstrate health awareness and keep up with modern trends; Tanita benefits by selling premium home devices and building brand association with wellness.
T2.why_behaviour_changes: Growing cultural emphasis on health and fitness as a lifestyle marker makes owning a device that measures body composition a way to signal personal commitment to health and keep up with peers.
T2.how_value_is_captured: Tanita can price home devices at a premium, sell through lifestyle retailers and online channels, and leverage brand storytelling to capture value by positioning the product as a status symbol rather than a pure health tool.
assumptions: Consumers value visible indicators of health and wellness.
Home use is acceptable for social signaling.
Price sensitivity is lower for status‑driven purchases.

frame.objective: Determine whether Tanita should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case based on its stand-on bioelectrical impedance body-fat analyser, leveraging evidence available up to 1993.
constraints: Limited to public sources published before 1993; no internal company data.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Uncertainty about Tanita’s current reach to individual buyers; must be discovered.
Investment decision must be justified by evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, or competitive advantage.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home fitness, weight management, or medical self‑monitoring).
2) Expand the existing B2B offering to additional health clubs or clinics without creating a consumer proposition.
3) No expansion – continue focusing exclusively on commercial scales and existing B2B customers.
4) License the bioelectrical impedance technology to third parties for consumer applications.

T1.claim: Health‑conscious consumers will purchase a stand‑on body‑fat analyser for home use because they view it as a medical necessity that provides actionable health insights.
T1.who_benefits: Consumers seeking to monitor body composition for health management; Tanita benefits by selling a premium product directly to consumers.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: Growing public awareness of the health risks of excess body fat (as indicated by medical evidence and media coverage) makes consumers seek tools that provide measurable data.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Tanita captures value through premium pricing and direct‑to‑consumer sales, leveraging its established medical credibility to justify higher margins.
assumptions: Consumers trust medical evidence linking body fat to health risks.
Tanita’s existing professional reputation transfers to consumer perception of accuracy.
Home use is feasible and convenient for target consumers.
predictions: Surveyed consumers will indicate willingness to pay at least 15% above the price of standard household scales for a body‑fat analyser.
Purchase intent will be higher among those who report tracking BMI or body composition for health reasons.
Sales will be concentrated in regions with higher obesity rates and higher health‑awareness.

T2.why_behaviour_changes: Growing interest in personal health and body composition as a status marker (driven by media, fitness trends, and peer influence) motivates consumers to buy tools that signal health expertise.
T2.how_value_is_captured: Tanita captures value through design differentiation, retail partnerships, and premium pricing, leveraging its existing brand reputation to command higher margins.

frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient evidence from public sources available as of late 2002 to justify ACR Electronics investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case built on its 406 MHz satellite distress-beacon technology.
constraints: Limited to public sources published on or before late 2002; no internal company data.
Investment justification must be based on evidence of consumer demand, market opportunity, or competitive advantage.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Current reach to individual buyers is unknown and must be discovered.
Evidence must address the specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation, emergency preparedness, remote work) and the technology's suitability for it.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation, emergency preparedness) using the 406 MHz distress-beacon technology.
2) Expand the existing B2B/industrial focus without targeting individual consumers (status quo).
3) Pursue a different route to market or customer group (e.g., partnering with outdoor retailers, offering a subscription service) while retaining the core technology.
4) No expansion: continue focusing on current markets and product lines.

T1.how_value_is_captured: ACR can capture value by selling the beacons directly to consumers through retail channels (outdoor gear stores, online) at a premium price, leveraging the technology’s safety reputation.
assumptions: Outdoor recreation market in the U.S. is large and growing in 2002.

frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient evidence from public sources available as of late 2002 to justify ACR Electronics investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case built on its 406 MHz satellite distress-beacon technology.
constraints: Limited to public sources published on or before late 2002; no internal company data.
Investment justification must be based on evidence of consumer demand, market opportunity, or competitive advantage.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Current reach to individual buyers is unknown and must be discovered.
Evidence must address the specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation, emergency preparedness, remote work) and the technology's suitability for it.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation, emergency preparedness) using the 406 MHz distress-beacon technology.
2) Expand the existing B2B/industrial focus without targeting individual consumers (status quo).
3) Pursue a different route to market or customer group (e.g., partnering with outdoor retailers, offering a subscription service) while retaining the core technology.
4) No expansion: continue focusing on current markets and product lines.

frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient evidence from public sources available as of late 2002 to justify ACR Electronics investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case built on its 406 MHz satellite distress-beacon technology.
constraints: Limited to public sources published on or before late 2002; no internal company data.
Investment justification must be based on evidence of consumer demand, market opportunity, or competitive advantage.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.
Current reach to individual buyers is unknown and must be discovered.
Evidence must address the specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation, emergency preparedness, remote work) and the technology's suitability for it.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation, emergency preparedness) using the 406 MHz distress-beacon technology.
2) Expand the existing B2B/industrial focus without targeting individual consumers (status quo).
3) Pursue a different route to market or customer group (e.g., partnering with outdoor retailers, offering a subscription service) while retaining the core technology.
4) No expansion: continue focusing on current markets and product lines.

arguments.claim: Outdoor recreation enthusiasts will adopt 406 MHz distress beacons because they provide a reliable emergency communication solution for remote environments where other methods (phone, radio) are unavailable.
arguments.who_benefits: Consumers who engage in high‑risk outdoor activities (e.g., hikers, climbers, remote workers) benefit from a device that can summon help in case of distress.
arguments.why_behaviour_changes: These users currently rely on unreliable means of communication and are willing to invest in safety equipment that offers a proven distress signal. The FCC’s approval of PLBs and the technology’s ability to transmit distress signals without
arguments.how_value_is_captured: ACR can capture value by selling the beacons directly to consumers through retail channels (outdoor gear stores, online) at a premium price, leveraging the technology’s safety reputation.
assumptions: Outdoor recreation market in the U.S. is large and growing in 2002.
Consumers are aware of the existence of 406 MHz distress beacons and understand their functionality.
Price sensitivity is moderate; a device that saves lives is valued even at a higher cost.
predictions: If offered in outdoor retail, at least 10% of surveyed hikers/climbers would express intent to purchase within 12 weeks.
Sales would be concentrated in regions with high outdoor activity density (e.g., national parks).

arguments.claim: Emergency preparedness households will adopt 406 MHz distress beacons because they provide a reliable backup communication solution for critical situations where primary phone or radio lines may be unavailable.
arguments.who_benefits: Consumers who live in remote areas, have limited access to emergency services, or rely on backup power sources benefit from a device that can transmit distress signals.
arguments.why_behaviour_changes: These households currently rely on outdated or unreliable methods (e.g., battery‑operated radios, signal mirrors) and are willing to invest in technology that offers a proven distress signal and FCC approval.
arguments.how_value_is_captured: ACR can capture value by selling the beacons through retail channels (hardware stores, online) at a premium price, leveraging the technology’s safety reputation and emergency‑focused marketing.
assumptions: Emergency preparedness market in the U.S. is significant and growing in 2002.
Consumers are aware of the existence of 406 MHz distress beacons and understand their emergency functionality.
Price sensitivity is moderate for safety‑critical devices.
predictions: If offered in retail, at least 15% of surveyed households in remote areas would express intent to purchase within 12 weeks.
Sales would be concentrated in regions with high remote housing density (e.g., rural communities, mountain regions).

alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation, emergency preparedness) using the 406 MHz distress-beacon technology.
2) Expand the existing B2B/industrial focus without targeting individual consumers (status quo).

X1.name: Consumer Preference Survey for Garden Tractor Purchase
X1.method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios. Recruit 500 U.S. homeowners (250 urban, 250 suburban) via a panel. Randomly assign participants to one of two scenarios: (A) price‑sensitive scenario emphasizing low cost and multiple‑use functionality; (B) status‑driven scenario emphasizing prestige, modern lifestyle, and brand image. Participants indicate their likelihood to purchase (1‑10) and the primary reason for purchase (multiple choice).
X1.sample: 500 U.S. homeowners (250 urban, 250 suburban) recruited via an online panel, stratified by geographic region.
X1.measure: Average purchase likelihood score (1‑10) and primary reason selection (price vs status).

prediction_by_theory.T1: In price‑sensitive scenario, average likelihood will be ≥ 7 and price/multiple‑use will be the top reason (selected by ≇ 55% of participants).
prediction_by_theory.T2: In status‑driven scenario, average likelihood will be ≥ 7 and status/prestige will be the top reason (selected by ≇ 55% of participants).

X1.decision_rule: If average likelihood in price‑sensitive scenario ≥ 7 and price/multiple‑use is top reason → T1 is more likely. If average likelihood in status‑driven scenario ≥ 7 and status/prestige is top reason → T2 is more likely. If neither scenario meets threshold → evidence insufficient to justify investment. final.target_customer: Homeowners with small gardens who need a versatile, low‑cost tool for multiple household chores.
final.value_proposition: A differentiated consumer product that leverages existing tractor engineering to serve small‑garden tasks, positioned as a practical, multipurpose utility item rather than a premium agricultural machine.
final.next_action: Run the consumer preference survey (Test X1) within the €15,000 budget and 10‑week timeline to test whether price‑sensitive demand exceeds status‑driven demand.
final.uncertainty: The exact size of the small‑garden household segment in 1962 and the relative importance of price versus status are unknown. Evidence on consumer motivations is limited to independent studies that do not quantify purchase decisions.

frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient evidence from public sources available as of mid-1962 to justify Deere & Company investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, leveraging its tractor engineering.

alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., small‑holder farming, hobby gardening, or a niche agricultural activity) using existing tractor engineering.

X1.name: Consumer Messaging Test: Practical vs Status Messaging
X1.method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Recruit 300 homeowners (150 urban, 150 suburban) who have small gardens. Randomly assign participants to one of two groups: Group A receives a product description emphasizing practical utility (multiple‑use functionality, low cost, ease of maintenance). Group B receives the same description plus a status‑driven narrative (modern lifestyle, prestige, signaling affluence). Both groups view the same product
X1.sample: 300 homeowners (150 urban, 150 suburban) with small gardens, recruited via an online panel to match 1962 demographics
X1.measure: Purchase intent measured on a 7‑point Likert scale (1‑Very unlikely to buy, 7‑Very likely to buy). Secondary measure: willingness to pay (WTP) on a 1‑10 scale. Primary outcome is the difference in average purchase intent between the two groups

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A (practical messaging) will have higher purchase intent and WTP than Group B (status messaging).
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B (status messaging) will have higher purchase intent and WTP than Group A (practical messaging).

final.target_customer: Homeowners with small gardens who value practical utility and low cost.
final.value_proposition: A lawn and garden tractor marketed as a versatile, inexpensive tool for multiple household chores, leveraging Deere’s existing dealer network to reach this segment.
final.next_action: Run the Consumer Messaging Test (X1) within the €15,000 budget and 10‑week timeline, randomizing participants to either practical or status messaging.
final.uncertainty: The evidence base is limited to a single source (deere-wheelhorse-demand) that supports a price‑driven, practical‑use motivation, but does not directly address status motivations. The test is needed to resolve this uncertainty.
would_change_if: If the test shows a significant difference in purchase intent between the two messaging frames, indicating a status‑driven segment. If the test shows no significant difference, reinforcing the current B2B model.
